mainEntity.name: Hermes / The Spirit Of Enterprise
mainEntity.description:
The flying bronze figure on the east wall of the Roger Stevens building is one of the most prominent, striking sculptures on campus. Originally it was commissioned by the Midland Bank for their London offices in the late 1950s. Chattaway called it Hermes, but the Greek god’s ‘less desirable’ associations, as the protector of thieves, led his patrons to rename it The Spirit of Enterprise.

In 1983, when the Midland building was sold to developers for £30m, it was rumoured that the sculpture was to be sold for scrap, and the dilemma hit the national press. The work was saved by Chattaway’s longstanding patron, Stanley Burton, who sent a cheque to the University of Leeds to purchase it for campus. Weighing four and a half tons, it arrived from London on a low-loader and was installed that June. Chattaway was delighted at the return of his original title, Hermes.

The blank wall is a perfect backdrop to display the sculpture to best advantage, a far cry from its position in London. In a very different new home, it is a dramatic example of how public art can change and adapt to new settings and new audiences, creating fresh dialogues with its environment.
